newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MASTERS A FAMILY MATTER FOR NICKLAUS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MASTERS A FAMILY MATTER FOR NICKLAUS.

text.p: Jack Nicklaus, responding to family presssure, shot a two-under-par 70 on Friday to avoid missing the cut in the Masters -- an ignominy he had suffered only three times in 38 previous appearances.

Nicklaus, who already owns a record six green jackets, was inspired by his son and Masters caddie Jackie to match his best round at Augusta National since 1995 as a birthday gift for another son, Steven.

Jackie, who caddied for his father the last time Nicklaus won the Masters -- in 1986 when he became the oldest winner -- told his father that he had to make the cut because Jackie had promised Steve that he would, as a present.
It started at the 15th hole, where Nicklaus had a 25-foot putt for eagle.
"As we were walking up to the green Jackie said 'You've got to make this. I promised Steve you'd make (the cut) for his birthday,'" Nicklaus related later.
"It went right in the centre of the hole," Nicklaus said of the putt that put him under par for the day.
But Jackie, who knew that his whole family was going to be in Augusta for the weekend, wasn't through.
On the 18th hole Nicklaus, who has two others sons and a daughter, faced another 25-footer, this time for birdie.
"Jackie said 'You've got to make this for 70,'" Nicklaus recalled.
"With this kind of putt I'm trying to figure out how to get down in two," he said.
"Anyway, it went right dead in the hole," Nicklaus said with a big smile.
"It was kinda fun to finish that way."
